proposals.evidence: DEDR2041: Telugu koncemu explicitly means a little or a few, and Kannada koñce a little; Tamil/Malayalam koñcam gives the related quantity noun. Pattapu koⁿcev matches the nasal-affricate sequence but has final v rather than the quoted m(u). This is a qualified family proposal requiring review of the final consonant, not an exact-form claim. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1931: Tamil cēppu is listed among redness forms and Malayalam cōppu means red/red colour. Pattapu ṣēpu preserves a long-vowel sibilant-p formation with plain single p; its retroflex sibilant remains unchanged. The article explicitly identifies Kodagu cōpï and related forms as Malayalam loans, so those are not treated as independent proof of inheritance or as an established Pattapu donor route. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4680 gives Telugu maṇṭa flame, blaze and Tamil maṇṭu to blaze up or glow. Pattapu maⁿta preserves the nasal-stop formation with its non-retroflex t and the broader source meaning fire retained. The whole article contains the relevant noun even though its Tamil head is verbal. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review; the Telugu comparison alone does not establish borrowing. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5276 explicitly gives Telugu baluvu heavy, great, strong and Kannada bolu strength, firmness, bigness. Pattapu boluvu preserves the b-l-v formation with a rounded first vowel; its heavy sense agrees with the Telugu noun/adjective, not merely the article’s strength head. The vowel difference and inheritance-versus-contact interpretation remain subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1851: Telugu kuṟuca explicitly means short, dwarfish, small, and Kannada kuṟucu/kuṟaci denotes smallness or dwarfishness. Pattapu kuɹasa is compared with this fuller sibilant-bearing formation rather than only the bare kuṟu stem. Its medial a and s in place of the Telugu u and c remain explicit sound differences; no unsupported suffix node is introduced. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
